title: Bivariate Data and Claims
summary: Set the hidden slope and scatter behind eight players' seasons; the scatter plot, best-fit line, prediction, and two-way table all follow.
narration: A coach claims that players who practice more make more free throws. One player cannot prove it, but a whole team's pairs of numbers can. In this chapter you plot those pairs, fit a line, read its slope as a rate, and use it to predict. Then you sort the same players into a two-way table and compare percentages, because with categories it is the percentages, not the raw counts, that reveal an association.

practice.prompt: A team's line of best fit is y = 3x + 11, where x is hours of practice per week and y is free throws made out of 50. How many free throws does the line predict for a player who practices 6 hours a week?
A line of best fit passes through the points (2, 20) and (6, 30), where x is hours of practice and y is free throws made. What is the slope of the line, in free throws per hour?
practice.explanation: Slope = change in y ÷ change in x = (30 − 20) ÷ (6 − 2) = 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5 free throws per hour of practice.

practice.prompt: A school surveyed students about sleep. Of the 40 students who play a school sport, 22 slept at least 8 hours last night; of the 25 students who do not play a sport, 15 did. Which comparison correctly tests the claim that playing a sport goes with getting at least 8 hours of sleep?
choices: 22 is greater than 15, so players slept at least 8 hours more often
55% of players versus 60% of non-players, so players slept at least 8 hours less often
40 is greater than 25, so players slept at least 8 hours more often
22 + 15 = 37, so about a third of the students slept at least 8 hours
practice.explanation: Compare the relative frequency within each row, not the raw counts. Players: 22 / 40 = 0.55 = 55%. Non-players: 15 / 25 = 0.60 = 60%. Since 55% < 60%, players slept at least 8 hours LESS often, even though 22 is the larger count; the rows have different sizes (40 and 25), so 22 vs 15 and 40 vs 25 compare nothing useful. Adding 22 + 15 = 37 out of 40 + 25 = 65 students is 37 / 65 = 56.9%, not a third, and it ignores the two groups entirely.
